text:
ConocoPhillips dipped less than 0.1% today after climbing 5.34% over the past two weeks, effectively holding near its recent highs. The flat move comes as oil markets remain caught between competing forces: crude prices have pulled back slightly (US oil at $96.24/barrel, down from earlier peaks), but the geopolitical backdrop—tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, hurricane disruptions to Gulf of Mexico production, and Middle East/Eastern Europe conflicts—continues to keep fuel supplies tight and support energy company margins.

The broader context is that the market has already priced in most of the near-term volatility. The Trump-Putin diesel deal announced yesterday and the Iran escalation are dramatic headlines, but they don't change the fundamental supply squeeze that benefits refiners and crude producers like ConocoPhillips. The stock's 5% rally over two weeks reflects recognition that damaged refinery capacity and supply disruptions are structurally bullish for integrated oil companies, at least in the near term.
